messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: [Action Required] Runway bridging & temporary GPU hold for Zenova - sizing ask

Marcus / Priyom -

Quick context: Zenova (Alyssa Ford) is now in final procurement review; they sign in ~4 weeks if exec legal clears. They're asking for a deterministic SLA and guaranteed node availability for initial go-live (Q4). Sales wants to request a short soft-hold on capacity while legal finishes the SOW to avoid losing the slot to competing demand.

Ask: can infra confirm a conservative sizing profile and whether we can patch a 30-day soft-hold (non-billable, revocable) for 16A100s-equivalent nodes in us-west for the Oct go-live runway? Attached is the sizing sheet they shared (I've redacted customer internal traffic patterns) - the highlighted tab is the expected token throughput.

What I need by EOD tomorrow:
- Marcus: feasible node set & any caveats (thermal/placement constraints)
- Priyom: risk note on perf delta if we need to allocate quantized variants or split across AZs
- Lauren: I'll loop you once we have numbers for the commercial ask + duration

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: zenova_runway_sizing_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action Required] Runway bridging & temporary GPU hold for Zenova - sizing ask

Mateo -

Thanks for the heads up and the sizing sheet. Quick read and initial notes below (keeping conservatively biased):

1) Baseline request: 16x A100-equivalent (40GB) nodes for steady-state inference with 500k tokens/min peak.

2) Feasibility: yes, but two important caveats:
  - Thermal affinity: the 16 nodes will need to be spread across two racks to avoid sustained thermal throttling; that increases cross-rack network egress (negligible for inference but ops needs to plan).
  - Pod packing: if we give a soft-hold now, we can reserve the physical slot mapping, but we can only guarantee the exact SKU family (40GB class) not the exact firmware build.

3) Alternatives/options:
  - Option A (recommended soft-hold): Reserve 16 nodes as non-billable soft-hold for 45 days. If they sign, convert to reserved dedicated pool.
  - Option B (flex): Reserve 12 nodes + burstable pool of 4 nodes as preemption-safe (lower-priced, quantized variants) — lower cost but potential 10-20% perf delta on tail latency.

4) Ops action & timeline: we can put a soft-hold within 24h but need an ops ticket (CAP-HOLD-957) and a confirm from Legal on the hold terms (revocable, no charges). Also suggest a two-week canary of 2 nodes in staging to ensure model swap behaves as expected before full allocation.

I'll attach a short runbook for the staging canary and the CAP-HOLD form.

Marcus
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runway_canary_playbook.md (txt), CAP-HOLD-957-form.pdf (pdf)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action Required] Runway bridging & temporary GPU hold for Zenova - sizing ask

Thanks Marcus - that matches my perf read from the evals. A few short notes from SE: 

- Quantized variants: performance is generally within 5-15% for median latency, but tail latency can spike depending on prompt length distribution. I recommend the staging canary Marcus mentioned and a short prompt-set smoke-test (we can run it against their sample workload in staging).
- AZ split: From an SLO perspective, split across two AZs is fine for availability but increases cold-start variability due to cross-AZ p95 differences; we'll need to instrument more aggressive request routing for even latency.

If Sales wants to push for Option A I suggest we also include one-time migration assistance and a 30-day post-activation SLA review as part of the conversion incentive (helps close).

Priyom
Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

All -

Sounds good. Mateo: please reply to Alyssa and CC me with the proposed Option A soft-hold (16 nodes, 45 days) + the staging canary plan. I'll attach a provisional MOU that documents the hold is non-billable and revocable. If Legal pushes back we can default to Option B.

I'll prepare the commercial terms once we have the ops ticket number (Marcus - please confirm CAP-HOLD-957 goes into the system so I can reference it in the MOU).

Mateo, once you send the external note, I'll follow with the MOU.

Lauren

Redwood Inference
